articles.title: Bob Myers Reveals Message to Jaylen Brown After 76ers-Celtics Trade, Emphasizes Leadership
articles.summary: Bob Myers, the President of HBSE Sports, revealed his message to Jaylen Brown after the Philadelphia 76ers added the five-time All-Star via trade from the Boston Celtics in July.
articles.body:
Bob Myers, the President of HBSE Sports, revealed his message to Jaylen Brown after the Philadelphia 76ers added the five-time All-Star via trade from the Boston Celtics in July.

Myers made his remarks to former NBA superstars Vince Carter and Tracy McGrady on The Cousins podcast .

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

The Philadelphia 76ers have made the playoffs eight of the last nine years but haven't advanced past the Eastern Conference semifinals. Last year's team upset the Boston Celtics in the first round of the playoffs but lost to the eventual NBA champion New York Knicks in the second round.

Philadelphia went all-in this offseason, however, trading Paul George and four draft picks for Brown and later adding LeBron James via free agency. They join a formidable trio featuring 2022-23 NBA MVP Joel Embiid, All-NBA Third Team member Tyrese Maxey and unanimous All-Rookie First Team member VJ Edgecombe.

It's a formidable lineup for a 76ers team searching for its first Eastern Conference title since 2001 and its first NBA championship since 1983.

Philadelphia has certainly added championship experience and veteran leadership to the team. James is entering his 24th NBA season and has 10 NBA Finals appearances and four NBA championships. Brown has played 10 seasons, with a pair of NBA Finals trips, six Eastern Conference Finals appearances and one title. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, a two-time NBA champion, is aboard as well and will be a key player off the bench.

It's clear from Myers' remarks that he valued Brown's past success and the leadership he can bring to the table. The same could go for James and KCP as well, as Philadelphia looks to finally take that next step.

articles.title: Juancho Hernangómez: "La selección pinta muy bien para los próximos años"
articles.standfirst: El madrileño, segundo capitán de la selección, protagonista en Radio MARCA
articles.summary: El madrileño, segundo capitán de la selección, protagonista en Radio MARCA
articles.body: Juancho Hernangómez vuelve a 'La Familia'. El alero madrileño afronta los importantes encuentros de clasificación para el Mundial 2027 ante Portugal y Grecia como segundo capitán del conjunto español y ejerciendo de padrino de los nuevos talentos que vienen como Aday Mara, Hugo González o Baba Miller. Desde la concentración de Zaragoza, atendió la llamada de 'El Programa de Ortega'. "Muchas ganas de jugar con ellos, ya les conocía desde hace años y ver cómo ha ido su progresión...vienen con muchas ganas y creo que pinta muy bien la selección para los próximos años, tienen mucho talento, son buenas personas, compiten", apuntó sobre los primeros días de preparación. El pasado Eurobasket, en el que España no consiguió pasar de la fase de grupos, supuso el fin de la era Scariolo y el nacimiento de la nueva generación con el concurso de Sergio De Larrea, Santi Aldama o Mario Saint Supery. Juancho no vivió sus mejores días en Chipre, una experiencia que le ha ayudado a crecer y mejorar. "Se pasa mal, pero no es de los peores momentos que he tenido en mi carrera deportiva. De todo se aprende. Creo que fue un campeonato para aprender. Yo tuve la suerte de llegar y tocar el cielo y ganar, pero cuando perdimos hablando con Rudy y Llull me decían que lo difícil es eso, es empezar, aprender, que los jóvenes vayan cogiendo experiencia...no pasa nada, de todo se aprende, las experiencias malas hay que vivirlas y para disfrutar las buenas hay que pasarlo mal. Hemos aprendido de ello y ahora tenemos un nuevo reto", comentó. Los hermanos Hernangómez ejercen desde el pasado verano como capitanes de la selección. Tomando el testigo de Sergio Llull y Rudy Fernández y con la misión de seguir manteniendo intactos los valores que identifican al baloncesto español. "Sigue siendo un sueño, para mi familia y para mí venir con la selección siempre ha sido nuestra prioridad, ganar con la selección ha sido lo más bonito que nos ha pasado en nuestra vida deportiva y no lo cambio por nada. Para nosotros sigue siendo especial, vengo con la misma ilusión de siempre y seguiré viniendo siempre que el seleccionador quiera. Sigo enamorado del baloncesto, sigo enamorado de jugar con mi hermano y es un sueño poder hacerlo en cualquier equipo", valoró. Juancho Hernangómez regresó hace tres temporadas a Europa procedente de la NBA. Recaló en el Panathinaikos de Atenas, que había configurado un proyecto de élite con Ataman en el banquillo para volver a la cima europea. Al madrileño le costó arrancar, pero desde el primer día es un ídolo en la ciudad y en la afición y acaba de renovar hasta 2031 pese a tener ofertas. "He encontrado un sitio donde soy muy feliz, la manera en la que viven el baloncesto...fue un primer año muy duro, pero lo ganamos todo y cuando ganas allí es historia. Me siento muy querido y apreciado. Que te quieran al final siempre es bueno, tenía un año más de contrato, sí que tenía ofertas de otros equipos y creo que Panathinaikos me iba a dejar salir y creo que lo mejor era mi continuidad allí a largo plazo, sintiéndome muy querido por la afición, el dueño y el entrenador y es una decisión que me ha gustado", contó. Desde la próxima semana se pondrá a las órdenes de la leyenda Zeljko Obradovic, que más de una década después, ha regresado al club ateniense para seguir agrandando su palmarés. Tendrá a su disposición a Juancho y a un auténtico equipazo para aspirar a todo. "Es la presión que vivimos en Panathinaikos, fichamos a lo mejor de lo mejor y no nos vale con llegar a una final, hay que ir a por títulos y ellos lo viven así, apostar fuerte por lo mejor que haya y ganar. No tenemos otra opción. Han traído a Obradovic, que es una leyenda, ha ganado 6 veces allí la Euroliga y tengo muchas ganas de aprender de él, hablé con él antes de mi renovación. A mí me guata aprender de los mejores". El alero se formó y creció en Movistar Estudiantes, con el que debutó y se convirtió en uno de los mejores aleros de la ACB. Su rendimiento le valió el salto a la NBA, pero el madrileño sueña con un final de carrera en 'casa'. "Yo siempre he dicho que me gustaría volver a Estudiantes y retirarme dónde empezó todo, pero al final las vidas cambian mucho. Claro que es un final soñado, pero nunca me esperaba jugar en Grecia y sentirme tan querido", finalizó.

articles.title: Hailey Van Lith Lands New WNBA Contract as Sun Make Roster Moves Ahead of FIBA World Cup
articles.summary: Hailey Van Lith will get another chance to prove herself in the WNBA this week.
articles.body:
Hailey Van Lith will get another chance to prove herself in the WNBA this week.

The Connecticut Sun announced Wednesday that Van Lith signed an "upgraded" seven-day contract with Leila Lacan set to fulfill her FIBA World Cup obligations for France.

Van Lith was the 11th overall pick in the 2025 WNBA draft after her tremendous college career and figured to be a serviceable player for years to come, but she's struggled to find her place in the league early on.

Sky Ban Enes Kanter Freedom from Home Games (AP)

After a disappointing rookie year with the Chicago Sky that was marred by a nagging ankle injury, Van Lith was waived by the team this May. The Sun picked her up off waivers the same day she was cut by the Sky.

Connecticut waived her a few weeks after picking her up, but she was brought back on a developmental contract in late May. She reportedly had other options in free agency but opted to stay with the Sun because she thought it was better for her overall growth as a player.

Van Lith has made 16 appearances with Connecticut this year, putting up 5.3 points, 1.9 assists and 1.0 rebounds per game in just over 14 minutes per contest.

The seven-day contract should be a good opportunity for Van Lith to show what she can do before the season ends. Considering Lacan was a starter who played nearly 30 minutes a game, Van Lith should get plenty of playing time.

She'll also have the chance to play without much pressure since the Sun are 10-27 and have already been eliminated from playoff contention. If Van Lith can provide valuable minutes off the bench, it could lead to another opportunity this offseason.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Fever vs. Sky Becomes Most-Watched WNBA Regular-Season Game in Nearly 3 Decades
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever made WNBA broadcast history during last Sunday's victory over DiJonai Carrington and the Chicago Sky.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever made WNBA broadcast history during last Sunday's victory over DiJonai Carrington and the Chicago Sky.

A total audience delivery of 3.31 million viewers tuned in to watch Clark scored 37 points in the Fever's 113-90 win, according to NBC Sports .

That marked the WNBA regular season's most-watched game since 1997 and the third most-watched game of all time, according to the network.

Sky Ban Enes Kanter Freedom from Home Games (AP)

The record for the most-watched WNBA regular-season game stands at 5.04 million total viewers from when the New York Liberty and Los Angeles Sparks opened the league's inaugural season on NBC in June 1997.

The second-most watched regular-season game stands at 3.59 million viewers, also from the 1997 opening weekend, according to NBC Sports.

Sunday's broadcast peaked at 3.82 million viewers who watched the Fever set a franchise record with 18 three-pointers, including eight from Clark and six from Kelsey Mitchell.

The game marked the WNBA's second NBC primetime broadcast of the season following a July 12 game featuring the Fever and Las Vegas Aces.

The Fever/Aces game averaged a total audience delivery of 2.64 million viewers to make it the second most-watched game of the season, according to NBC Sports .

NBC Sports has so far averaged a total audience delivery of 1.75 million viewers for seven WNBA games aired on NBC and Peacock this season, the network reported.

The WNBA playoffs tip off Sept. 27. Semifinal and Finals coverage will be provided on NBC and Peacock as well as Disney Networks and USA Network, according to the league .

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom sends letter to WNBA requesting review of Sky ejection incident, full ticket refund
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom sent a letter to the WNBA demanding answers after security removed him from his courtside seat during a Chicago Sky game.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE: Enes Kanter Freedom is demanding answers from the WNBA after security removed him from his courtside seat during Sunday’s game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena. Freedom attended the game wearing a shirt advocating for the protection of women’s sports, days after announcing his intention to enter the WNBA Draft as a form of protest. During the third quarter, Sky guard Natasha Cloud crossed the court and confronted Freedom as he sat near the baseline. In a letter sent to WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert, Freedom requested an explanation for his removal and accused the league of applying its policies selectively. Freedom called the ejection an "apparent selective enforcement of League and arena policies that raises serious concerns of viewpoint discrimination," according to the letter obtained by OutKick. The former NBA first-round pick also disputed claims from Chicago Sky co-owner Nadia Rawlinson and nearby spectators that he instigated the confrontation with Cloud. "Late in the third quarter, Chicago Sky player Natasha Cloud turned from the court, approached my seat, and began yelling, cursing, and pointing in my direction," Freedom wrote. "Security and Sky personnel intervened, and I was subsequently escorted from the arena." Freedom argued that the league appeared to apply a double standard because Cloud had not been publicly reprimanded or punished for her actions. SKY COACH PRAISES NATASHA CLOUD AFTER HEATED VERBAL ALTERCATION WITH ENES KANTER FREEDOM "According to the WNBA, any physical or verbal altercation with a fan is treated as conduct detrimental to the game," Freedom wrote. "The WNBA Office holds the authority to issue heavy fines or multi-game suspensions for players who cross the line into berating or cursing at spectators. Yet Ms. Cloud’s conduct of yelling, swearing, and pointing at a spectator (me) appears to have escaped any accountability and was, in fact, defended by her coach." Freedom also disputed the contention that his own conduct warranted removal from the arena. "Meanwhile, I remained fully aware that I could not step onto the court and ensured my presence and expression complied with applicable standards," the letter states. "In other words, I followed your rules." Freedom further argued that security failed to follow the WNBA’s stated process for addressing alleged fan misconduct. WNBA ADMITS SECURITY IN ATLANTA WAS WRONG TO MAKE FANS COVER SHIRTS AT DREAM-FEVER GAME "According to the WNBA Fan Code of Conduct, a spectator should be issued a warning for any alleged violation before being forced to leave the game," Freedom wrote. "I received no such warning prior to my ejection." The letter repeatedly alleged that Freedom received unfair treatment because of his public advocacy and the message displayed on his shirt. "The circumstances of my removal only further highlight a pattern and practice of the League applying its rules unfairly," Freedom wrote. "For example, why did arena personnel believe my ejection was warranted while Ms. Cloud appears to have escaped any accountability for clearly violating League rules against the use of profanity and insults directed at fans?" Freedom specifically questioned whether his advocacy "for defending the integrity of women’s sports" or his announcement that he intended to enter the WNBA Draft played a role in the decision. "I should not be treated differently because the League, its players, or personnel disagree with my viewpoint," Freedom wrote. "The timing and circumstances of my removal beg a variety of questions: Did my WNBA Draft announcement, prior communications with the League, public advocacy for women’s sports, or the message displayed on my shirt play a role in the decision to eject me?" Freedom also connected his removal to other recent controversies involving spectators who expressed opposition to allowing transgender athletes to compete in women’s sports. "On July 28, spectators outside the Seattle Storm v. Indiana Fever game were treated differently based on their viewpoints," Freedom wrote. "While supporters of women’s sports were told they could not rally on the raised platform outside the arena, transgender activists were allowed to do so." "Next, on August 16, spectators at an Atlanta Dream v. Indiana Fever game were instructed to cover shirts supporting women’s sports that were like mine, while allowing pro-transgender shirts to remain. Although the WNBA subsequently acknowledged that the intervention ‘should not have happened,’ it was no more than a week later that I was removed from the August 23 WNBA game wearing a shirt expressing a similar viewpoint." Freedom argued that those incidents "raise significant questions about the WNBA’s application of its own rules depending on the perceived viewpoints of its spectators." "It goes without saying that when I purchase a ticket to attend a WNBA game, I expect that I will not be discriminated against based on my viewpoint," Freedom wrote. Freedom requested "a written response within five business days" addressing five specific demands: "1. Identify the policy, rule, directive, or instruction relied upon in treating certain spectators, including me, differently when we express a viewpoint that appears unpopular with the WNBA; "2. Identify whether the decision to eject me was made or requested by WNBA personnel, Chicago Sky personnel, Wintrust Arena personnel, security personnel, or another individual or entity; "3. Confirm whether Ms. Cloud’s conduct has been or will be reviewed under any League policy governing player interactions with fans, including rules governing altercations that require player suspension, and state what accountability, if any, she, her team, and management will face; "4. Provide a full refund of the cost of my courtside tickets; and "5. Preserve all materials relating to this incident, including relevant video footage, incident or security reports, communications concerning my attendance or removal, communications referring to my WNBA Draft announcement or public advocacy for women’s sports, and any applicable policies or event-day directives." Freedom concluded the letter by warning that the controversy would not be resolved without a clear explanation from the league. STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW! "The pattern of viewpoint discrimination against those, like me, who advocate for the protection of women and integrity of women’s sports has created a real and substantial conflict that must be addressed," Freedom wrote. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The letter now puts the decision directly before Engelbert and WNBA leadership. Freedom is asking the league to identify who ordered his removal, explain the rule he allegedly violated and determine whether Cloud’s conduct merits a formal review. Until the league responds, the circumstances surrounding his ejection — and whether his political advocacy played any role in it — remain disputed. The Sky and WNBA have not responded to a request for comment on Freedom's letter.

articles.title: New Steph Curry Rumors Update Warriors Contract Extension Talks Ahead of Eligibility Date
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star point guard Stephen Curry is reportedly expected to receive a new payday soon.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star point guard Stephen Curry is reportedly expected to receive a new payday soon.

Curry becomes eligible for a contract extension on Saturday, and ESPN's Anthony Slater reported that team sources confirmed that he and the Warriors "are expected to engage with a mutual desire to keep Curry with the Warriors for the entirety of his career."

Curry is set to make $62.6 million this season in the final year of his previous deal, and he's eligible for an extension of up to two years and $136.7 million. Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy expressed confidence earlier this month that the two-time NBA MVP won't be going anywhere anytime soon.

"Ultimately it's his call, his decision, whether that's allowing his contract to run out and move on," Dunleavy said. "Look, if he comes to me and wants to be moved, [controlling owner] Joe [Lacob] and I will talk it through. We wouldn't love it. But he's earned the right to do what he wants. But as far as the messaging or any idea that he'd be anywhere else, that's not a thing we're looking at or he's looking at."

The Warriors have had a relatively quiet offseason after failing to land any of the big-name players they pursued. Golden State focused on bolstering its depth over the last few weeks, and the team signed veteran power forward Georges Niang and reserve guard Brandon Williams to one-year deals on Wednesday.

While the Warriors aren't expected to contend for a championship this year, Curry's loyalty to the team likely will ensure that he will remain the face of the franchise for the foreseeable future.

articles.title: Draymond Green Questions If Klay Thompson Will Fit with 'Heat Culture' After Signing Contract
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green weighed in on former teammate Klay Thompson signing with the Miami Heat following his departure from the Dallas Mavericks.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green weighed in on former teammate Klay Thompson signing with the Miami Heat following his departure from the Dallas Mavericks.

"I found it interesting when I saw they said, 'Klay going to Miami,'" Green said on The Draymond Green Show (0:36 mark). "I was like, 'Oh, that Heat Culture thing.' I don't know how that's going to work for Klay because Klay moves to the beat of his own drum. It's no maliciousness to it, it's just who Klay is and I want to see how that fits into 'Heat Culture' stuff. And so I'm looking forward to seeing how that happens."

Michael Jordan expected to leave media role

Thompson agreed to a two-year, $11.5 million contract with Miami on Sunday.

Green and Thompson were previously teammates on the Warriors from 2012-24, winning four championships together while playing alongside Stephen Curry.

Thompson has been known for his laid-back personality and affinity for being on his boat . He was reportedly late for his introductory press conference with Miami after getting stuck in traffic.

Meanwhile, Heat president Pat Riley has been a proponent of the "Heat Culture" philosophy. The hard-working, professional mindset has been a staple of the organization and featured on a jersey in the past.

Thompson revealed that he was excited to join the culture of his new organization

"We were talking about the conditioning test last night," Thompson said Tuesday, per Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel . "So I'm happy I've got five weeks to really prepare. I've got to get my treadmill back operating. But I'm really excited just to be pushed on a fitness level that I know will be so beneficial for me for this next season.

"A lot of players warn me about how tough it is, but I like hard stuff like that. I've been through harder things. Coming back from those injuries was harder than any conditioning drill or game I had to play. In a weird way, those injuries prepared me for uncomfortable feelings and tough times. Now I take it head on and embrace them."

Thompson is coming off a 2025-26 season with Dallas in which he averaged 11.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game while shooting 39.3 percent from the field and 38.3 percent from three-point territory.

articles.title: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation changes the lives of over 7,500 Oakland students through literacy programs
articles.summary: NBA News: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player and the four tie NBA champion, could be a force to be reckoned with on the court but both and hi.
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player and the four tie NBA champion, could be a force to be reckoned with on the court but both and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have remained devoted to their foundation, Eat. Learn & Play. The high profile couple recently celebrated their foundation celebrating seven years of changing lives in Oakland and now, they have marked a new achievement.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat. Learn & Play, make a major difference in bridging the literacy gap in OaklandJust a few days ago, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat. Learn & Play, made an update about how the charity has tried to close the literacy gap in Oakland.The heartfelt post reads as, “When a child learns to read, everything changes. Curiosity takes off, and a whole world opens up. That’s why, in 2024, Eat. Learn. Play. pledged $25 million over five years to close Oakland’s literacy gap, working toward 10,000 tutoring opportunities by 2029. To date, our 1:1 and small group tutoring has reached over 7,500 students in the Oakland Unified School District.”The post added, “Personalized support layered on top of classroom instruction with students building confidence one page at a time. We’ve also placed more than 1 million books into Oakland kids’ hands with the @Oaklitcoalition and through programs like our free holiday book boxes and book fairs, and the Eat. Learn. Play. Bus.”The post has sparked chaos among fans as many remain in awe of how Stephen Curry and his wife Ayesha Curry have remained dedicated to helping thousands of children belonging to their hometown, Oakland.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have been public about helping more and more children to be educated in their hometownSeven years ago, the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, had only one goal in their lives as they set out to help and be there for children coming from underprivileged families and impoverished backgrounds.Both of them set up Eat. Learn & Play with a goal to provide nutritious meals and quality education across children in Oakland.A few months ago, in an interview with NPR's Scott Simon, Ayesha Curry opened up about why there was a literacy gap in their hometown as she said, “A lot of times, the students come into the school system, and their parents can't read at home. And so, of course, when their parents, you know, are not reading to them and nurturing them in that way as much as they want to, they don't have that option.”The popular entrepreneur added, “And then you just have kids just, you know, learning at a different pace. And when you're within the public school system, you don't always have the option to have, you know, that one-on-one time with the books and an educator the way that you need to in order to progress.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The one NBA ROTY edge Grizzlies' Cameron Boozer has vs. Darryn Peterson, AJ Dybantsa
articles.summary: ESPN has Grizzlies' Cam Boozer winning the 2027 NBA ROTY over Jazz's Darryn Peterson and Wizards' AJ Dybantsa.
articles.body:
A good barometer of an NBA Draft Class' depth is how close the Rookie of the Year race is. Plenty of names are in the mix to take home the award, but about five stand out. Among them, Cameron Boozer of the Memphis Grizzlies is the favorite to win the award, per ESPN's Summer Forecast. What edge does he have over Darryn Peterson of the Utah Jazz and AJ Dybantsa of the Washington Wizards ? Let's break it down.

Grizzlies' Boozer edges out Dybantsa, Peterson for NBA ROTY race in ESPN's Summer Forecast

Heading into the 2026 NBA Draft, there was no clear order for who would land in the top five, but a short list of names was already guaranteed to do so. Those same players will now have to duke it out for the NBA ROTY race. Five names stand above the rest: Memphis Grizzlies' Cameron Boozer, Sacramento Kings ' Darius Acuff Jr., Chicago Bulls ' Caleb Wilson, Utah Jazz 's Darryn Peterson, and Washington Wizards ' AJ Dybantsa.

How do all of these NBA ROTY candidates stack up against each other? ESPN forecasted one slim favorite, with an ingrained edge that his team has and no other squad offers.

Notably, the frontrunners are the same people who were drafted first, second, third, and fourth overall. Acuff Jr. is also the only one with the highest odds outside of the top five picks to land on the list.

Among all of them, why does Boozer have a five-point difference that sets him apart?

It all has to do with the Grizzlies and the minutes they can afford him so he can develop.

"These players all landed in situations that should be beneficial from an early usage and minutes standpoint, but it's Boozer who should have the biggest role of the three, with Memphis likely to orient its operation around him for the foreseeable future as it needs an offensive player who can shoulder a scoring load and connect teammates. On paper, he looks like the slight favorite," ESPN declared.

Boozer will be handed the keys to the Grizzlies, a luxury that his other NBA ROTY competitors will not be afforded. This is because Ja Morant left for the Portland Trail Blazers , and the Grizzlies are focusing on their young guys rather than being forced to compete.

Peterson, for instance, will likely be benched often if his performances don't pan out, making way for guys like Ace Bailey , Keyonte George , and Lauri Markkanen . The same goes with Dybantsa, who is pressured to perform immediately alongside Trae Young and Anthony Davis for a postseason spot in a cutthroat Eastern Conference.

Wilson might have the most leeway in development, which could threaten Boozer's NBA ROTY win. Even then, he cannot be as ball-dominant as he was back with the UNC Tar Heels. This is because guys like Norman Powell , Josh Giddey , Matas Buzelis , Patrick Williams , and Rob Dillingham have something to prove to the Bulls organization.

The Grizzlies immediately get to start Boozer at the power forward spot ahead of guys like Taylor Hendricks and GG Jackson . Other players on their roster also don't need any sort of heliocentrism to be effective. Boozer gets complemented well with the two-way prowess of teammates like Scotty Pippen Jr. , Cedric Coward , Jerami Grant , and Zach Edey .

When all of these considerations are put into place, it's not hard to see why the Grizzlies will get their third NBA ROTY winner after Pau Gasol and Ja Morant. Will any unseen contender step up to usurp expectations and beat Boozer by the end of the year?
